data.title: Adani seeks government nod to invest in airlines, eyes bigger role in India's aviation market
data.description:
Adani Group has approached the government seeking permission to invest in the airline sector, signalling a possible expansion of its aviation interests beyond airport operations as it sees scope for a significant increase in India's air traffic capacity.

Group chief financial officer Jugeshinder Robbie Singh said on Friday that India needs nearly 10 times its current daily flight capacity, to around 30,000 flights, to cater to the potential passenger base.

"And that's why we requested the government to at least allow us to invest, so that we can facilitate the development of airlines. Some fund, some other airline company and things like that...or an entrepreneur who wants to go into that space," Singh told reporters on the sidelines of the India Debt Capital Market Summit.

Adani sees room for more airlines

Singh said more than 60 crore people in India have the potential to fly, pointing to the need for greater airline capacity to accommodate the country's untapped aviation demand.

The group's request comes amid calls for greater competition in India's airline industry, which has effectively become a duopoly dominated by Tata Group-owned Air India and Rahul Bhatia-led IndiGo. The two carriers together control around 90% of the domestic aviation market.

Operational disruptions at IndiGo last year, which triggered thousands of flight cancellations, also fuelled demands for more airlines and greater competition in the sector.

Earlier denials of airline ambitions

The latest comments come despite the group's earlier indications that it was not looking to enter the airline business directly.

In July this year, the Adani Group had said it was "not evaluating any proposal to enter the airlines business". On November 3, Adani Airport Holdings chief executive Arun Bansal had also ruled out an airline venture, arguing that competing with customers was never a good strategy.

The group operates eight airports across India, including Mumbai, Navi Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Lucknow and Guwahati. Its airport network handles more than a fourth of the country's air passenger traffic, giving it a substantial presence in India's aviation infrastructure.

Singh's remarks, however, suggest the group is seeking a broader role in the airline ecosystem, potentially by enabling investments in existing carriers, funds or entrepreneurs looking to enter the sector.<meta content="cms.article3" name="cmsei-article3"/> For Reprint Rights: timescontent.com

data.title: Volkswagen being singled out, rivals also paying 10% tax for parts imports, says German automaker
data.description:
MUMBAI: German automaker Volkswagen (VW) told a Mumbai court that rival companies, including BMW, Mercedes-Benz and Kia are also importing car parts into India at a 10% customs duty, arguing it has been unfairly singled out in a $1.2 billion tax dispute, Reuters reported on Friday.

In a court filing dated November 10, VW's India unit, Skoda Auto Volkswagen India, said the government's contention that other carmakers paid 30% duty while it alone paid 10% was "factually incorrect". The tax demand against the company "deserves to be quashed" if other automakers are allowed to follow the same import model, it argued. To support its case, VW submitted a table citing 2024 import data for BMW, Mercedes-Benz, Kia, Isuzu Motors and JSW MG Motor. BMW had 390,360 major shipments of car components during the year, while Mercedes-Benz had 80,972, all imported under the lower tariff category, Reuters reported citing a court filing.

VW maintained its rivals import components for assembling vehicles in India, much like it does, and that it is being selectively targeted. However, it would need to establish that its competitors' imports were similarly used to assemble complete vehicles to strengthen its argument, Reuters reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

VW is challenging a record tax demand over allegations that it deliberately imported components in separate consignments at 10% duty and assembled them into complete cars in India, thereby avoiding the higher tariffs of around 30% applicable to car kits.

Indian tax authorities have described the company's conduct as one of "fraud and subterfuge". VW has denied any wrongdoing, warning that the demand could wipe out its investments in India, where it has about 2% market share.

The Mumbai court is scheduled to hear matter on Monday. It is likely to rule initially only on whether tax authorities were entitled to scrutinise company's imports going back 12 years. The dispute highlights continuing concerns among foreign investors over India's tariff regime, with prolonged investigations and litigation creating uncertainty for businesses.<meta content="cms.article3" name="cmsei-article3"/> For Reprint Rights: timescontent.com

data.title: S&P cuts Tata Motors PV ratings on weaker JLR margins, poor cash
data.description:
Mumbai: S&P Global Ratings on Friday downgraded the credit ratings of Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles (TMPV) and its wholly-owned units, stating weaker-than-expected operating performance at Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) is weighing on total profits and cash flows. The rating agency lowered its long-term issuer credit rating on TMPV and unit TML Holdings to 'BBB-' from 'BBB', while revising the outlook to stable from negative. It cut JLR's rating to 'BB+' from 'BBB-', also with a stable outlook against a negative outlook earlier.

"Weak profitability and negative free operating cash flow (FOCF) at Jaguar Land Rover Automotive PLC will likely delay financial recovery at Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles," S&P said.

British luxury carmaker JLR, which contributes about 80% of TMPV's consolidated revenue, is expected to remain a drag on the Indian automaker's earnings. S&P estimates TMPV's adjusted Ebitda margin will improve marginally to about 0.4% in FY27 from 0.2% last year.

The agency expects JLR to face continued pressure from weak sales volume and challenging market conditions. Sales of imported vehicles in China fell 35% year-on-year in the first half of FY27, further clouding the automaker's recovery prospects. S&P has pushed back its expectation of JLR turning free cash flow positive to FY28 from FY27, citing the weaker operating environment.

JLR's financial performance has also been hit by restructuring-related costs and a major product portfolio refresh.

The company reported exceptional items of 530 million in the September quarter, including separation costs and write-downs of intangible assets under development. It has lowered its full-year revenue guidance to 25 billion and expects a pre-tax margin of 2-3%, citing geopolitical risks and restructuring costs.

S&P expects JLR's annual capital expenditure and research and development spending to remain elevated at 3.3-3.4 billion over FY27 and FY28 as it undertakes the portfolio refresh. This is expected to result in adjusted negative FOCF of about 1.4 billion in FY27.<meta content="cms.article3" name="cmsei-article3"/> For Reprint Rights: timescontent.com

data.title: Centre floats urea import tender ahead of next sowing season
data.description:
New Delhi: India's National Fertilizers has invited bids for the import of urea, as the government seeks to ensure timely availability of the key fertiliser for the upcoming sowing season.

The tender, issued on behalf of the Department of Fertilizers under the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers on November 27, seeks offers with preference for the earliest arrivals into India. According to the notice inviting tender, shipments from loading ports must be completed by January 31, 2027.

The deadline for submission of bids is December 8, 2026. The import tender comes amid the government's efforts to maintain adequate fertiliser supplies for farmers. Urea is the most widely consumed fertiliser in India and is heavily subsidised by the centre.<meta content="cms.article3" name="cmsei-article3"/> For Reprint Rights: timescontent.com

data.title: Adani Group plans capex increase, aims higher domestic borrowings
data.description:
Mumbai: Adani Group plans to invest an aggregate of Rs 2.20 lakh crore in the current fiscal ended March 2027, up from Rs 1.56 lakh crore last fiscal group Chief Financial Officer (CFO) of the Adani Group is Jugeshinder Singh said. The group has planned market borrowings of Rs 1.3 lakh crore to Rs 1.4 lakh crore each broadly for the current and next fiscal year, Singh said.

"We can invest close to Rs 2.20 lakh crore which is largely constrained by the fact that (we cannot) complete that much on the ground, we don't have the capability. In fact the country as a whole will take time to build that ecosystem...the health systems, the education systems, the core manufacturing, cold storage systems. We need to build out the core infra which we are not building at fast enough speed that the country needs," Singh said.

The group plans to borrow Rs 1.3 lakh crore to Rs 1.4 lakh crore borrowing in the next fiscal year ended March 2028 which is broadly the same as they borrowed in the current fiscal year, Singh said.

Singh said the group will be ready to demerge its airports business in the next fiscal year after which the board will decide when to go for an IPO. Adani Airport Holdings Limited (AAHL), owns, operates, or holds majority stakes in eight airports across the country.

Singh said the airports business is now ready to fund its own investment plan and the group wants its non aero revenue which is money earned through commercial or non flight activities to be about 65% of total revenues before it can be demerged.

"The non-aero income broadly where we want to see in terms of percentage. So it's going in the right direction. As as those business cases solidify more over the next six months to nine months, with non-aero on average somewhere between 60-65%, then yes (we can demerge)," Singh said adding its roughly just around 60% now.

Singh said the company will continue to borrow from the domestic and overseas markets with both Adani Power and Adani Enterprises likely to tap the domestic market for a public issue of rupee bonds next fiscal.

Another group company Adani Ports also will likely tap the overseas market for a 20 year dollar bond next fiscal year, Singh said.

"It will mostly be for refinance though they do have enough cash to just retire the debt. There is a $600 million maturity coming too so we will replace some (debt) with. (But) we want to issue some long dated paper (too)," Singh said.

The group expects gross debt on its books to be broadly between 3 to 3.2 times EBITDA (earnings before interest tax depreciation and amortisation) which is about Rs 3.9 lakh crore.

The Adani Group aims to increase the percentage of domestic borrowings to close to 80% from 56% currently.

"Ultimately infra is domestic and we have to create wealth for domestic participants so they must we should create opportunities for them to participate," Singh said.

For its data centre business Singh said has bank lines of $3 billion out of which $900 million has been raised and $10 billion is likely to be raised in the next four years.<meta content="cms.article3" name="cmsei-article3"/> For Reprint Rights: timescontent.com

data.title: 'We wish them well': Adani Group CFO on Tata Group's ongoing leadership and listing row
data.description:
Adani Group CFO Jugeshinder 'Robbie' Singh wished the Tata Group well amid an intensifying boardroom rift over the proposed listing of Tata Sons and the reappointment of N Chandrasekaran as its chairman, saying he hoped India's largest conglomerate would continue to grow, PTI reported on Friday.

"We wish them well," Singh told reporters in Mumbai, describing the Tatas as a "storied" group when asked about the recent developments within the conglomerate, the report said.

Singh said the Adani Group wanted every Indian company to expand and hoped domestic businesses would eventually account for half of the Fortune 500 list. "The Adani Group wants every Indian corporate to grow," he said.

The remarks come ahead of the November 30 Tata Sons board meeting, with differences between Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata and the company's management centred on Chandrasekaran's proposed reappointment for a third five-year term and the holding company's listing.

The Reserve Bank of India has mandated a public listing of Tata Sons after classifying it as an upper-layer non-banking financial company (NBFC), while Noel Tata has proposed restructuring it as an operating company to avoid the requirement.

At the September 17 board meeting, four directors, including Tata Trusts nominee Venu Srinivasan, backed Chandrasekaran's continuation, while Noel Tata was the sole dissenter.<meta content="cms.article3" name="cmsei-article3"/> For Reprint Rights: timescontent.com

data.title: Exelon Crews Mobilize to Support Customers and Restore Power During and After Severe Thanksgiving Storm
data.description:
Exelon and its operating companies mobilized employees, contractors and mutual-assistance resources during Thanksgiving as a powerful nor’easter brought damaging winds, heavy rain and coastal flooding to parts of the Mid-Atlantic, causing widespread damage and power outages.

The storm swept across the Mid-Atlantic, leaving hundreds of thousands of customers without service across BGE, PECO, Atlantic City Electric, Delmarva Power and Pepco territories. As of early Friday afternoon, the vast majority of those outages had been restored quickly and safely. Exelon continues to direct additional resources to the areas with the most severe damage to restore power to customers still without service.

"Our customers count on us every day, and that responsibility takes on a special meaning during the holidays, when families are gathering and communities are depending on us," said Mike Innocenzo, Exelon’s Chief Operating Officer. "Thousands of Exelon employees, contractors and partners have answered the call this holiday to safely restore power in the communities where they live and work. I want to thank them for being there for our customers and their neighbors when it matters most, and for staying on until the work is done."

Working around the clock for customers and their families

Across the Mid-Atlantic, crews from BGE, PECO, Atlantic City Electric, Delmarva Power and Pepco continue to work around the clock to restore power quickly and safely in some of the storm’s harshest conditions. Coastal wind gusts reached speeds as high as 70 mph in parts of New Jersey, Delaware and Maryland, while several inches of rain and flooding brought down trees, limbs, poles and wires and closed roads, limiting safe access to some of the hardest-hit areas. Exelon is moving resources to where they are needed most, including ComEd mutual assistance personnel and resources from the Chicagoland area that have traveled east to reinforce the hardest-hit communities.

Always on, with safety first

Throughout our service territories, dedicated employees work around the clock, preparing before storms, responding when conditions are at their worst and staying on the job until every customer is restored. Safety remains our top priority. Exelon and its utilities urge customers to stay away from downed wires and always assume they are energized. Customers should report outages and check their local utility's website or mobile app for the latest restoration information.

About Exelon

Exelon () is a Fortune 200 company and one of the nation’s largest utility companies, serving almost 11 million customers through six fully regulated transmission and distribution utilities — Atlantic City Electric, BGE, ComEd, Delmarva Power, PECO, and Pepco. Exelon’s more than 20,000 employees dedicate their time and expertise to supporting our communities through reliable, affordable and efficient energy delivery, workforce development, equity, economic development and volunteerism. data.title: South America eyes $18 billion gas, power integration plan, study says
data.description:
A study backed by regional development bank CAF and the Latin American Energy Organization (OLACDE) on Friday identified 17 infrastructure projects worth $18 billion that would create an integrated natural gas and electricity market across six South American countries.

The plan, covering Mercosur trade bloc members Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay, and Uruguay, as well as Bolivia and Chile, aims to unlock up to $4.5 billion in net economic benefits for the region and create more than 200,000 jobs by 2035, according to findings presented in Montevideo.

  • Gas interconnections carried 22 million cubic meters daily in 2025, 29% of their capacity

  • The study evaluated 11 integration routes, 7 of which depend on Argentina's Manuel Belgrano pipeline to move gas from the country's Vaca Muerta shale formation

  • The route to central Chile offered the highest cost savings relative to required investment compared with importing liquefied natural gas (LNG), the study found

  • The Argentina-Brazil pipeline corridor via Bolivia offers the largest potential impact, the study added, though its competitiveness hinges on Argentine export duties, Bolivian transit fees, and Brazilian transport tariffs

  • Under a limited-budget scenario, upgrading Argentina's Northern Gas Pipeline would require $2.4 billion in additional investment to yield $4.3 billion in net regional benefits

  • The study recommended advancing via pipelines, so countries can sign long-term stable contracts while negotiating a regional framework treaty

SINGAPORE, Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Phaos Technology Holdings (Cayman) Limited (NYSE American: POAS) ("Phaos" or the "Company") today outlined an opportunity to develop automated car wash and vehicle care services in Southeast Asia, particularly in Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand. The Company is evaluating Singapore and Malaysia as initial markets for services that combine convenience for drivers and fleet operators with automation and water reuse. In a second phase, it may consider expanding into other Southeast Asian markets.

Singapore had more than 650,000 cars in October 2026, including nearly 99,000 private-hire cars, according to Land Transport Authority data1. In Malaysia, the Malaysian Automotive Association2 reported 630,461 new passenger vehicles sold from January through October 2026, up about 4% year over year. Separately, Grand View Research3 estimates that Malaysia's broader car wash services market could grow from US$208.9 million in 2025 to US$361.7 million by 2033, a projected annual growth rate of 7.3% from 2026 to 2033. The forecast covers multiple wash formats and does not estimate revenue for Phaos.

In Indonesia, Ken Research4 estimates that paid professional car wash services could grow from US$390 million in 2025 to US$686 million in 2032, or 8.4% annually. In Thailand, a nationwide National Statistical Office survey5 put 2023 receipts for businesses classified under car washing, polishing and similar services at THB 14.1 billion. In October 2026, Bangchak6 reported Lodon JetX automated washes at 50 of its fuel stations, showing adoption of the format. The two market figures cover broader service categories and do not measure Phaos's addressable revenue.

Phaos is exploring the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to automate car washing, with the aim of reducing labor costs and improving water recycling. In Singapore, Inchcape reported that the automated gantry it developed with Kärcher can recycle up to 85% of the water used per wash.7

"We see an opportunity to serve vehicles that need regular care," said Gan Hong Loon, Chief Executive Officer of Phaos. "Singapore and specific regions in Malaysia give us places to test demand and site economics before we consider expanding."

GIG HARBOR, WA / ACCESS Newswire / November 27, 2026 / IP Strategy Holdings, Inc. (the "Company" or "IP Strategy") today announced that it received a notification letter from The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC ("Nasdaq") dated November 24, 2026, advising the Company that, because it has not yet filed its Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q for the period ended September 30, 2026 (the "Form 10-Q"), the Company is not currently in compliance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5250(c)(1).

Nasdaq Listing Rule 5250(c)(1) requires listed companies to timely file all required periodic financial reports with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

The Nasdaq notification has no immediate effect on the listing of the Company's common stock on Nasdaq. However, if the Company fails to timely regain compliance with the Listing Rule 5250(c)(1), the Company's common stock will be subject to delisting from Nasdaq.

Under the Nasdaq Listing Rules, the Company has 60 calendar days from the date of the notification, or until January 23, 2027, to submit to Nasdaq a plan to regain compliance. If Nasdaq accepts the Company's plan, Nasdaq may grant the Company an exception of up to 180 calendar days from the original due date of the Form 10-Q, or until May 24, 2027, to regain compliance. If Nasdaq does not accept the Company's plan, then the Company will have the opportunity to appeal that decision to a Nasdaq Hearings Panel.

The Company is diligently working to complete and file the Form 10-Q and intends to take the necessary steps to regain compliance with Nasdaq's continued listing requirements in December 2026.

data.title: Annovis Bio Receives NYSE Notice Regarding Continued Listing Standard
data.description:
MALVERN, Pa., Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Annovis Bio, Inc. (“Annovis” or the “Company”), a Phase 3 clinical-stage biotechnology company developing buntanetap, an investigational once-daily pill for neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and Parkinson’s disease (PD), today announced that on November 25, 2026, it received written notice from the New York Stock Exchange (the "NYSE"). The notice states that the Company is not in compliance with Section 802.01C of the NYSE Listed Company Manual. That section requires the average closing price of a listed company's common stock to be at least $1.00 per share over a consecutive 30 trading-day period. As of November 24, 2026, the 30 trading-day average closing price of the Company's common stock was $0.93.

The Company has six months after receiving the notice to regain compliance with the minimum share price requirement. During that time, the Company's common stock will continue to be listed and traded on the NYSE under the symbol "ANVS," with a ".BC" indicator showing that the Company is below the NYSE's continued listing standards. The Company will regain compliance if on the last trading day of any calendar month during the cure period its closing share price is at least $1.00 and its average closing share price over the 30 trading days ending that day is also at least $1.00.

The Company intends to notify the NYSE within the required 10 business days of its intent to cure the deficiency. The Company intends to monitor the closing price of its common stock and to consider all available options to regain compliance, which may include a reverse stock split, subject to stockholder approval.

As previously disclosed, on October 29, 2026, the Company received a separate notice from the NYSE because its average global market capitalization over a consecutive 30 trading-day period was below $50 million and, at the same time, its stockholders' equity was below $50 million. The Company remains subject to the conditions in that notice. The cure periods under the two standards run independently of each other.

The NYSE notice does not immediately affect the listing or trading of the Company's common stock. The notice also does not affect the Company's business operations or its reporting obligations with the Securities and Exchange Commission, and it does not conflict with or cause an event of default under any of the Company's material debt or other agreements.

About Annovis

Headquartered in Malvern, Pennsylvania, Annovis Bio, Inc. is a Phase 3 clinical-stage biotechnology company developing treatments for neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's disease (AD) and Parkinson's disease (PD). The Company's lead drug candidate, buntanetap (formerly posiphen), is an investigational once-daily oral therapy that inhibits the translation of multiple neurotoxic proteins, including APP and amyloid beta, tau, alpha-synuclein, and TDP-43, through a specific RNA-targeting mechanism of action. By addressing the underlying causes of neurodegeneration, Annovis aims to halt disease progression and improve cognitive and motor functions in patients. For more information, visit www.annovisbio.com and follow us on LinkedIn, YouTube, and X.

These include statements about the Company's intent and ability to regain compliance with the NYSE's continued listing standards, the potential actions it may take to do so, and the continued listing of its common stock on the NYSE.
